questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An isolated physical system transitions from initial state parameter $p_i = 6$ to final configuration $p_f = 12$ while conserving the quantity $\mathcal{E} = p_i^2 + 2p_f$. What is the value of $\mathcal{E}$ in SI units?
questions.explanation: Apply the conservation & invariant balance principles in Laws of Motion (Atwood Machine & Pulleys).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two coupled particles of equal mass carry linear momenta in the ratio $1 : 7$. If the slower particle has kinetic energy $K_0 = 7\text{ J}$, what is the combined kinetic energy of the two-particle system?
questions.explanation: Apply the conservation & invariant balance principles in Laws of Motion (Friction on Inclined Planes).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A dynamical coordinate evolves with time $t$ according to $y(t) = 8t^2 - 8t$ (in SI units). Determine the instantaneous rate of change $\frac{dy}{dt}$ at $t = 2\text{ s}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the instantaneous rate & gradient law principles in Laws of Motion (Circular Banking).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The potential energy of a particle moving along the $x$-axis is given by $U(x) = 2x^3 - 54x\text{ J}$. At what positive position $x > 0$ does the net conservative force on the particle vanish?
questions.explanation: Apply the instantaneous rate & gradient law principles in Laws of Motion (Pseudo Force & Wedge Constraints).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two geometrically similar physical elements have characteristic linear dimensions in the ratio $L_2 / L_1 = 3$. If a response quantity $R$ is proportional to $L^2$, find the ratio $\frac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the boundary ratio & scaling analysis principles in Laws of Motion (Atwood Machine & Pulleys).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When the amplitude of the driving excitation in a linear resistive medium (resistance $11$ units) is multiplied by $4$, by what factor does the rate of quadratic energy dissipation change?
questions.solution: Quadratic dependence on the excitation amplitude yields a $4^2 = 16$-fold increase.
questions.explanation: Apply the boundary ratio & scaling analysis principles in Laws of Motion (Friction on Inclined Planes).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A physical quantity $f(z)$ increases linearly from $0$ to $24$ units over the interval $z \in [0, 5]$. Evaluate $\int_0^{5} f(z)\,dz$.
questions.solution: Area of the right triangle under the linear curve is $\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 24 = 60$.
questions.explanation: Apply the graphical slope & area integration principles in Laws of Motion (Circular Banking).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A linear calibration line has slope $13$ and vertical-axis intercept $-6$. At what value of the horizontal coordinate does the output cross zero?
questions.explanation: Apply the graphical slope & area integration principles in Laws of Motion (Pseudo Force & Wedge Constraints).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A physical observable $Z$ is related to independent measurements $A$ and $B$ by $Z = A^{7} B^{-2}$. If the relative error in $A$ is $1\%$ and in $B$ is $14\%$, what is the maximum percentage error in $Z$?
questions.explanation: Apply the dimensional & exponent homogeneity principles in Laws of Motion (Atwood Machine & Pulleys).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A dimensionless product is constructed as $\Pi = P^x Q^{8} R^{-1}$. If dimensional consistency requires the exponent relation $2x - 8 + 1 = 0$, find $x$.
questions.explanation: Apply the dimensional & exponent homogeneity principles in Laws of Motion (Friction on Inclined Planes).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two coherent harmonic disturbances of amplitudes $A_1 = 16$ and $A_2 = 2$ superpose at a point. What is the ratio of the maximum possible resultant intensity to the minimum resultant intensity?
questions.explanation: Apply the two-source superposition & phase principles in Laws of Motion (Circular Banking).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two mutually perpendicular vector components in a plane have magnitudes $F_x = 9$ and $F_y = 12$. Find the magnitude of their resultant vector and the cosine of its angle with the positive $x$-axis.
questions.explanation: Apply the two-source superposition & phase principles in Laws of Motion (Pseudo Force & Wedge Constraints).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A cyclic device absorbs $180\text{ J}$ of energy from a high-temperature source per cycle and rejects $36\text{ J}$ to a low-temperature sink. What is its thermal efficiency?
questions.explanation: Apply the energy efficiency & dissipation principles in Laws of Motion (Atwood Machine & Pulleys).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An interaction reduces the mechanical energy of a body to $\frac{1}{5}$ of its initial value $E_0 = 95\text{ J}$. How much mechanical energy is lost during the interaction?
questions.solution: Dissipated energy $\Delta E = E_0 - E_0/5 = 95 - 19 = 76\text{ J}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the energy efficiency & dissipation principles in Laws of Motion (Friction on Inclined Planes).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For a mechanical assembly to remain stable, the stiffness parameter $k$ must exceed the critical value $k_c = 20\text{ N/m}$. If the operating stiffness is set to $k = 46\text{ N/m}$, what is the excess stiffness margin $k - k_c$?
questions.solution: The stability margin is $k - k_c = (46) - 20 = 26\text{ N/m}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the critical threshold & equilibrium principles in Laws of Motion (Circular Banking).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Three coplanar forces keep a point mass in static equilibrium. If two of the forces are mutually perpendicular with magnitudes $21\text{ N}$ and $7\text{ N}$, what is the magnitude of the third force?
questions.explanation: Apply the critical threshold & equilibrium principles in Laws of Motion (Pseudo Force & Wedge Constraints).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The frequency response function $H(\omega) = \frac{176}{\omega + 8^2 / \omega}$ for $\omega > 0$ reaches its maximum value at $\omega = \omega_0$. Determine $\omega_0$ and $H(\omega_0)$.
questions.solution: By AM-GM, $\omega + 8^2/\omega \ge 2(8)$ with equality at $\omega_0 = 8$, giving $H_{\max} = \frac{176}{2\cdot 8} = \frac{22}{2}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the resonance & extremum condition principles in Laws of Motion (Atwood Machine & Pulleys).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A DC source of EMF $E = 46\text{ V}$ and internal resistance $r = 23\,\Omega$ is connected across a variable load resistance $R_L$. Find the value of $R_L$ and the maximum power delivered to the load.
questions.explanation: Apply the resonance & extremum condition principles in Laws of Motion (Friction on Inclined Planes).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two particles $P_1$ and $P_2$ move along the $x$-axis with velocities $+24\text{ m/s}$ and $-3\text{ m/s}$ respectively relative to the ground. What is the speed of $P_1$ relative to $P_2$?
questions.explanation: Apply the relative frame & coupling constraint principles in Laws of Motion (Circular Banking).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two bodies $A$ and $B$ are connected by an inextensible constraint such that their displacements along their respective axes satisfy $x_A + 4x_B = \text{constant}$. If body $B$ has acceleration $+25\text{ m/s}^2$, what is the magnitude of the acceleration of body $A$?
questions.explanation: Apply the relative frame & coupling constraint principles in Laws of Motion (Pseudo Force & Wedge Constraints).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A physical quantity decays exponentially with time according to $N(t) = N_0 e^{-t/\tau}$, where $\tau = 26\text{ s}$. At what instant $t$ does $N(t)$ become equal to $N_0 e^{-5}$?
questions.explanation: Apply the transient decay & time constant principles in Laws of Motion (Atwood Machine & Pulleys).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A state variable approaches its steady-state value $Q_\infty = 162$ units according to $Q(t) = Q_\infty(1 - e^{-t/\tau})$ with $\tau = 6\text{ s}$. Evaluate the initial rate $\left.\frac{dQ}{dt}\right|_{t=0}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the transient decay & time constant principles in Laws of Motion (Friction on Inclined Planes).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A uniform vector field $\vec{F} = 28\hat{i} + 7\hat{j}$ passes through a flat surface element of area vector $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$ (in SI units). Calculate the flux $\Phi = \vec{F}\cdot\vec{A}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the flux, field & uncertainty analysis principles in Laws of Motion (Circular Banking).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The radial field magnitude at distance $r$ from a point source is given by $E(r) = \frac{1856}{r^2}$ (in SI units). Find the field magnitude at $r = 8\text{ m}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the flux, field & uncertainty analysis principles in Laws of Motion (Pseudo Force & Wedge Constraints).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A dynamical invariant is given by $I = m v^2$ with $m = 6$ and $v = 6$ in SI units. Calculate the numerical value of $I$.
questions.explanation: Apply numerical conservation law in Laws of Motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The position coordinate of a particle varies with time as $s(t) = 7t^3 + 7t$ (in SI units). Find the instantaneous speed $\frac{ds}{dt}$ at $t = 2\text{ s}$.
questions.explanation: Apply numerical rate & gradient evaluation in Laws of Motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two cascaded linear stages have amplification factors $G_1 = 10$ and $G_2 = 9$. What is the overall amplification factor $G_{\text{net}} = G_1 G_2$?
questions.explanation: Apply numerical ratio & scaling factor in Laws of Motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A position-dependent force $F(x) = 18x\text{ N}$ acts on a particle along the $x$-axis from $x = 0$ to $x = 2\text{ m}$. Calculate the work done in Joules.
questions.explanation: Apply numerical work & area integration in Laws of Motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The potential energy of a particle along the $x$-axis is $U(x) = (x - 13)^2 + 30\text{ J}$. What is the minimum potential energy (in J) attainable by the particle?
questions.solution: Since $(x - 13)^2 \ge 0$, the minimum potential energy is $30\text{ J}$.
questions.explanation: Apply numerical extremum & threshold in Laws of Motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A uniform field $\vec{E} = 11\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ crosses a planar area vector $\vec{S} = 3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 11\hat{k}$ (in SI units). Compute the scalar flux $\vec{E}\cdot\vec{S}$.
questions.explanation: Apply numerical flux & field magnitude in Laws of Motion.
